fns.desc: l2_packet_send() builds io[1].iov_base = &dst_addr (address of the local `const u8 *dst_addr` PARAMETER itself, a stack slot holding a pointer) instead of (u8 *) dst_addr (the actual 6-byte MAC address it points to, as correctly done for `buf` two lines below at io[3]). This sends ETH_ALEN=6 raw bytes of the pointer's own in-memory representation to the wpa_priv privileged helper as the 'destination address' field, not the real MAC address -- a genuine data-corruption bug in the CONFIG_PRIVSEP build, silent (no crash, no NULL-deref) but functionally wrong every time l2_packet_send() is used with privilege separation enabled.

copy_sta_he_capab()'s guard chain calls check_valid_he_mcs(hapd, he_capab, opmode) BEFORE ieee80211_invalid_he_cap_size(he_capab, he_capab_len) validates the actual received length. check_valid_he_mcs() takes no length parameter at all and unconditionally reads sta_mcs_set[i*4] (i.e. bytes at offset IEEE80211_HE_CAPAB_MIN_LEN(17)+i*4 into the peer-supplied buffer, for i up to mcs_count-1 which can be 1-3 depending on the AP's OWN configured channel width) via WPA_GET_LE16 at ieee802_11_he.c:450-452. he_capab/he_capab_len come directly from the STA's wire-supplied HE Capabilities IE (elems->he_capabilities / elems->he_capabilities_len in ieee802_11.c:5463-5555, attacker-controlled length). A malicious/malformed STA sending an HE Capabilities IE shorter than 17+mcs_nss_size bytes (e.g. exactly the 17-byte mac+phy-capab minimum, omitting the MCS set entirely) causes an out-of-bounds read past the actual received IE buffer before any length check runs -- a real CWE-125 buffer over-read on attacker-controlled wire data, exactly the class of bug the FN read-through was asked to hunt for.
